slides.quote: My friend had her whitening done here — hers looks incredible. Will mine?

truth.text: Same gel, same lamp — two clinics, visibly different results. The chemistry never changes between offices. The workflow does.

answer.text: If the outcome depends on who happens to be working that day, you have a whitening lottery. A strict, standardized protocol ends the lottery.

slides.notes: 03 Hook (hook). Opening quote or question, ‘The hard truth’ card and ‘The fläsh answer’ card. Labels can be changed per slide.

slides.title: 1 mm. Green. Neutral pH.

points.text: Mix fresh — full potency protected until the moment of mixing.
You see every surface covered — the gel turns clear as oxygen releases.
Oxidation of chromogens at a neutral pH — never corroding the enamel.
A thin, starved layer produces a pale patch — Sin #5.

slides.notes: 05 Points (points). The standard slide: 2–4 points, each with a short lead and an explanation of about 14 words. Optional focus box on the right (points then narrow to 900 px).

slides.title: Soft Tissue First

points.lead: Vitamin E or vaseline on the lips.
points.text: Then the fläsh lip retractor, docked onto the lamp head.
For the patient and for every team member present.
Dry gingiva; only slight overlap onto cervical enamel; cure until solid.

slides.caption: Lamp docked on the lip retractor · filtered goggles
slides.notes: 06 Points + Photo (points_photo). 2–4 points plus photo (2:1) with caption. Without a photo file, a placeholder with the photo brief appears.

slides.title: The Lamp: Position Is Power

points.text: Patient at 45°, lamp head locked on the retractor — intensity level IIII.
One centimetre of gap costs ≈50% of the power.
Blue 460 nm light, absorbed by the green gel — no UV, no infrared, below 39 °C.

chart.title: Light power at the enamel
chart.note: 1 cm of extra gap ≈ 50% less light power (3² = 9 vs 4² = 16)

slides.notes: 07 Points + Chart (points_chart). 2–4 points plus a bar card (2–4 bars, values 0–100, one bar highlighted) with an optional note.

slides.text: Gel, lamp and fläshcard engineered as one closed system · WHITEsmile
slides.notes: 08 Statement (statement). One big number or keyword, a statement line and a short explanation.

slides.title: The Seven Sins of Isolation
items: No lip protection — vitamin E or vaseline
Barrier not properly placed or cured
Patient left unattended — no signal agreed

focus.title: Burns are never caused by the gel.
focus.text: Rescue: vitamin E or vaseline onto the gingiva — no panic, protocol.

slides.notes: 09 Checklist (checklist). Up to 7 numbered items, optional focus box.

slides.title: The Fix & The Conversation

steps.title: Re-isolate, correctly
steps.text: Rebuild the barrier and confirm the retractor is docked on the lamp head.

steps.title: Fresh 1 mm gel
steps.text: Full-thickness layer on the canines and cervical thirds — the lagging zones.

steps.title: Spend banked minutes
steps.text: The cycle time the fläshcard saved becomes a targeted touch-up.

steps.title: Say the words
steps.text: “The canines are always last. The white areas are temporary.” Book the one-week photo.

slides.caption: Repeat 3× (max 4×) — fresh gel each cycle, suction only, never rinse.

steps.title: Suction off the gel — no rinsing

slides.title: Oxidation, Not Erosion

left.label: Myth
items: The lamp works by heating the tooth

right.label: Fact
items: Oxidation of chromogens at neutral pH
Blue 460 nm light, below 39 °C — a photochemical effect
Burns are never caused by the gel — isolation prevents them

slides.title: “The Uneven Case”
slides.story: A 38-year-old at the end of cycle 3 — centrals magnificent, cervical thirds still yellow, canines two steps behind, chalky patches on the laterals. She is holding the mirror.

findings.cause: Gel layer below 1 mm in zones — Sin #5
Lamp gap or tilt — 1 cm ≈ −50% power

slides.notes: 17 Case (case). Case story (up to three lines) and up to 5 findings, each with its cause in one line.

slides.question: Cervical thirds still yellow after cycle 3 — what is the most likely cause?
slides.explanation: The barrier covered the cervical enamel — the gel never touched it. Re-isolate correctly, then apply fresh 1 mm gel.
slides.notes: 18 Quiz (quiz). Question with three answers; the build adds the answer slide with the highlighted option and the explanation.
